title: Stock market holiday: Is US stock market closed or open today for Labor Day 2025? | Stock Market News
content: The United States stock markets will remain closed on Monday, 1 September 2025, in observance of Labor Day, according to the official holiday list of the Nasdaq Stock Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE). Because the market is closed on Saturday and Sunday, there is no half‑day trading session preceding the holiday. Official NYSE data indicates that only two other holidays will occur in 2025: Thanksgiving on 27 November and Christmas on 25 December. The S&P 500 closed 0.64% lower at 6,460.26 points on Friday, down from 6,501.86 points at the previous close. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.15% to 21,455.55 points, compared with 21,705.16 points previously. title: 2025 Wrap-Up | bubbleinfo.com
content: In 2023, the number of property listings reached a low point, but a 17% increase in 2024 provided welcome relief, accompanied by a 5% rise in sales. By 2025, the market appears to have reached equilibrium, as a 7% increase in listings (161 additional homes) resulted in only 18 more sales. Instead, 201 more sellers canceled or withdrew their listings, likely due to frustration with a market that is not meeting their price expectations. Of the 887 unsuccessful sellers in 2025, most are expected to re-enter the market in 2026. The January listing surge is projected to create a 'flood' in some areas, with the number of homes for sale on February 1st expected to match the typical May/June inventory—half of which will be repeat listings from prior years. With 30 days remaining before the market effectively shuts down for Thanksgiving and the rest of 2025, the next few weeks may present a 'sneaky hot' opportunity for transactions.

title: Borse ai massimi: si avvicina il momento buono per vendere?
content: The stock market is experiencing strong performances worldwide, reaching new historical highs in the US (S&P500). However, despite the current momentum, there are signs of weakness beneath the surface. No market growth phase is infinite, and this one is no exception. While there is no current pessimism, things could change by next autumn, a time when it would be wise to be liquid or even short on stock market indices. Several factors suggest this scenario may unfold, with the analysis focusing on the US market, but with global repercussions if the US market were to decline. As one analyst notes, 'it's possible that the current upward trend could continue for a while, but it's also a good time to consider selling in a strong market, as no growth phase is infinite.'
